<p class="white-text">

Welcome to the <strong>Forest Insect and Disturbance Lab</strong> at Utah State University! Our research is focused on how weather, climate, and landscapes affect forest insect herbivores, disturbances, and forest ecosystems. We are especially interested in identifying the mechanisms of <strong> where, when, and how</strong> population irruptions by native forest insect herbivores start to better forecast future outbreaks. 

</p>

---

### Research Themes 

A) exploring the mechanisms of insect population irruptions at local and landscape scales

B) quantifying and identifying native and invasive threats to healthy forests in Utah and beyond

C) modeling the consequences of insect-caused disturbance and climate change across forested ecosystems

D) exploring forest dynamics in a changing world

E) expanding our toolbox for explaining and forecasting climate change impacts across ecosystems and continents

---

### Lab Ethos

We believe that:

A) science is for everyone! 

B) safety and well-being are vital for success

C) transparency and accountability improve teamwork

D) science is meant to be shared

E) self-improvement is nonlinear, but continuous
